summary:
The classic next-permutation algorithm was inverted when searching for the successor: it looked for `perm[j] < perm[i]` instead of `perm[j] > perm[i]`. This caused it to swap with a smaller element and produce a lexicographically earlier permutation. Changing the comparison to `>` restores the correct behavior, matching the documented example `[3,2,4,1] -> [3,4,1,2]`.

RESULT: FIXED
